newsitem.title: UK: Britain invites bids for Thameslink rail franchise.
newsitem.headline: Britain invites bids for Thameslink rail franchise.

text.p: Britain's Office of Passenger Rail Franchising (Opraf) said on Tuesday it had issued invitations to tender for the Thameslink passenger train operating company.
The deadline to lodge indicative bids for the line, the 23rd of Britain's 25 train operating companies to reach this stage of privatisation, is November l.
Thameslink serves regional centres north and south of London via the only rail lines through the city centre. Its passenger revenue was 76 million stg in the year to March 31, 1996.

Opraf said it expected the contract would be let with compensation arrangements in place to help the franchisee cope with the anticipated service disruption from the proposed construction of a high-speed rail link into central London from the Channel tunnel, and from the Thameslink 2000 project to increase the line's capacity.
Thirteen franchises have been awarded to private operators, mainly linked to British bus companies, since the franchising process moved to the contractual stage in autumn last year.
